title: Metal Organic Framework-Derived Metal Phosphates as Electrode Materials for Supercapacitors

nodes.label: Supercapacitor electrodes need higher specific capacitance and rate capability than pristine Ni-MOF provides
Replacing Ni-MOF's BTC linkers by phosphate should keep the MOF rod template while raising conductivity and capacitance
Ni-BTC MOF (tetraaqua-Ni units linked by BTC, H-bonded network) chosen as precursor and template

requires_unseen: 1D zigzag chain topology of Ni-MOF (F1 linked text)
attrs.image_note: Scheme 1 draws Ni-BTC coordination with H-bonds; chain topology is not drawn.

nodes.label: Hydrothermal treatment of Ni-MOF with sodium phosphate to substitute BTC by phosphate units

attrs.image_note: Scheme arrow labelled 'Sodium phosphate / Hydrothermal Synthesis'; product drawn as Ni-O-P network.

nodes.label: Hydrothermal ligand substitution converts Ni-MOF into MOF-derived NixPyOz
BTC carboxylate linkers are replaced by PO4 units (P-O, O-P-O bonds) in NixPyOz
NixPyOz is largely amorphous with weak nickel phosphite (Ni2(PO3)4) features, unlike crystalline Ni-MOF

requires_unseen: phase name nickel phosphite Ni2(PO3)4 behind card 04-010-2575 (F3 linked text)

nodes.label: NixPyOz keeps the Ni-MOF micro-rod outline, with expanded rods and rough, loosened surfaces

requires_unseen: panel a = Ni-MOF, panel b = NixPyOz (caption only; panels carry no sample names)

nodes.label: NixPyOz electrode film is more conductive than Ni-MOF film

requires_unseen: four-point-probe sheet resistances 1049.42 and 714.13 ohm/sq (F4 linked text)

nodes.label: NixPyOz electrode has lower charge-transfer resistance and faster ion diffusion than Ni-MOF
Phosphate substitution loosens the rods and raises conductivity, shortening ion paths and lowering charge-transfer resistance

requires_unseen: authors' attribution in F4 and F5 linked text

nodes.label: Charge storage in both electrodes is diffusion-controlled Faradaic Ni(II)/Ni(III) redox (pseudocapacitive)

requires_unseen: Ni(II)/Ni(III) assignment of the redox pair (F5 linked text)

nodes.label: NixPyOz reaches ~1620 F/g at 1 A/g, about four times Ni-MOF (~400 F/g)
NixPyOz keeps ~64% of its capacitance from 1 to 20 A/g versus ~21% for Ni-MOF
NixPyOz retains ~54% capacitance after 10,000 cycles with ~100% coulombic efficiency
MOF-derived NixPyOz from ligand substitution outperforms Ni-MOF in conductivity, capacitance and rate capability as supercapacitor electrode
BTC carboxylate stretches 1565/1436/1373 cm-1, coordinated water 1624 cm-1; P-O stretch 1120-910, O-P-O bend 600-530 cm-1
Smaller Nyquist semicircle means lower charge-transfer resistance; steeper low-frequency rise means faster ion diffusion
Specific capacitance from galvanostatic discharge: C = I dt / (m dV)
A redox peak pair whose current grows with sweep rate indicates diffusion-controlled Faradaic storage
JCPDS card 04-010-2575 (nickel phosphite) reference reflections
Loosely bound structures shorten ion diffusion length, raise ion uptake and accommodate redox volume change
Ni-MOF carboxylate bands (1565, 1436, 1338 cm-1) and 1624 cm-1 water band are absent in NixPyOz

Panel checks: F5d caption names MOF and NixPyOz but plots one set (NixPyOz by capacitance); F5e caption names NixPyOz only but plots both; F5e retention label 19% vs 84/399.3 = 21%; F2a label 1338 cm-1 vs text 1373; TGA text 7% loss at 450-550 C vs ~2-3% in trace; XRD phase match to JCPDS 04-010-2575 is weak (broad humps only).
